messages:
Maria: Quick sync — Q2 hosted GPU demand vs our reserved commitments looks like it may gap in eu-west1. Dashboard shows a median 14% delta day-over-day for the last 7 days. Anyone seeing the same on their side?
Jonathan: yup saw that spike yesterday afternoon, likely due to two customers onboarding large embedding jobs.
Li: running a short-run forecast now. Preliminary: if current onboarding continues we need ~120 extra A100-hours/day in eu-west1 by mid-May.
Sam: are those A100s reserved or on-demand? We should check committed pool vs burst buffer.
Maria: committed pool is 200 A100-equivalent in eu-west1, but effective throughput drops when <80% utilization because we can't bin-pack tiny requests.
Ashley: finance flagged a billing uptick in hosted for eu-west1 in last invoice (linked): https://billing.internal/reports/eu-west1-2026-02 — cost up ~18% MoM.
OpsBot: [alert] Billing anomaly: committed-hours usage 92% over last 72h; overage risk if trend continues.
Li: sharing the quick table I used:
```
SELECT date, sum(gpu_hours) as used, committed_hours
FROM forecast
WHERE region = 'eu-west1' AND service = 'hosted'
GROUP BY date
ORDER BY date DESC
LIMIT 14;
```
Result shows weekend troughs then big weekday spikes — demand is bursty, not smooth.
Jonathan: two options: 1) bump committed capacity (costly/capacity lead time), 2) change routing policy to prefer other regions for non-latency-sensitive workloads. Thoughts?
Sam: routing is possible but customers in EU require EU data residency. We can route embeddings to eu-west2 if latency ok. Capacity there has slack.
Maria: can we add a temporary burst offset (reserved pool short-term) or use preemptible instances for non-critical batch embeddings?
Ashley: finance prefers temporary over-committing long-term. If we can keep extra for <30 days and avoid a 12mo commitment that'd be ideal.
Li: sketched three scenarios attached inline: "conservative" keep current+10% buffers; "hedge-short" add 100 hours/day for 30 days; "commit-12mo" add 200 reserved devices. Hedge-short has best cost/benefit if onboarding rate plateaus after month.
Jonathan: operational constraints: adding reserved capacity in provider X has 10–14 day lead time. Preemptible approach could be immediate but increases tail latency and occasional failures.
Maria: immediate action items: (1) Li to finalize 30-day hedge numbers with hourly granularity, (2) Sam to test eu-west2 fallback for embeddings with <100ms added latency budget, (3) Ashley to model invoice vs hedge cost and threshold for converting to a 12mo commit.
Li: will share the CSV forecast by EOD. I'll put the most-likely scenario and 90% CI.
Sam: I'll run a small traffic-shift test to eu-west2 this afternoon (5% traffic) and post perf numbers.
Ashley: if we do hedge-short, finance will approve up to $Xk as long as there's a rollback plan and tagging for cost center.
OpsBot: [task created] #inc-alloc-196789: run eu-west2 failover test (assigned: Sam)
Maria: thanks — keep updates in this thread. If numbers worsen we may need emergency EC call. :warning:
